label: geotropic
definition: An orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's growing or bending downwards, towards or into the ground, in response to gravity.
reason: Floras use it for fruits and inflorescences that turn down to the ground or into it, as in geocarpic legumes. No PATO or FLOPO orientation term means this; PATO_0104035 pendent describes hanging, not growing towards the soil.
Bark splitting lengthwise is fissured bark. For valves and fruits the phrase describes dehiscence (FLOPO:0991149 dehiscent), so the rule should be limited to bark.
nonreticulate = not marked with a network: the negation of FLOPO:0991100 reticulate.

label: hypostomatic
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a leaf or leaf lamina by virtue of its stomata being confined to its abaxial (lower) surface.
reason: This is a standard leaf-anatomy character with no PATO or FLOPO term. Writing it as 'stomata present' on the lower epidermis would lose the absence from the upper surface. It belongs beside FLOPO:0991332 paracytic.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (two values of one margin: papillose FLOPO:0991059 and toothed)
reason: This is a compound of two values: the margin is minutely toothed and the teeth are papilla-like. It should become two qualities of the margin, not a new term.
Orchid lateral sepals pointing forward project straight out from the flower. FLOPO:0991382 porrect already has 'projecting forward' as a related synonym.
Tubercles or a midrib that are 'low-rounded' are slightly raised in a rounded dome, which is convex. 'Low' is a degree and stays in the record.

target: not increased thickness (PATO_0000591) [bearer: leaf lamina margin PO_0025009]
reason: The bearer is the margin and the quality is negated 'thickened', which is an exact synonym of PATO_0000591 increased thickness.
'Inflorescence compound-cymose' says what kind of inflorescence it is: a compound cyme. PO_0030126 already covers dichasium and pleiochasium as synonyms.
A petal without a lamina lacks its blade, which is an absence of a part (pattern 15). PO has no class for the petal blade itself, so the general lamina is used as part of the petal.
'Many-leaved' is an indefinite count of leaves on the bearer, like 'few-flowered'.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md: tomentose (PATO_0002341) on the part; star shaped (PATO_0002065) on its trichomes (trichome PO_0000282)
reason: Two values with different bearers: the part is finely tomentose and its hairs are stellate. It should not become one compound term.
PATO_0040009 bowl shaped is a concave 3-D shape in the form of a bowl.
'Stalked glandular' is the English wording for stipitate-glandular: covered with stalked glands.

target: percurrent (FLOPO:0991163) [bearer: keel ridge of the sepal or bract]
reason: 'Keel extending to apex' says the keel runs the whole length to the apex, which is percurrent. The keel here is a ridge of the sepal or bract, not PO_0025327 keel (the keel petals of a pea flower), so that PO class must not be used.
Antesepalous stamens stand opposite the sepals, so this is a relational position towards another part. In '6 antesepalous' the word also qualifies a count.
Unlike the rejected bare 'covered', this phrase names what covers the part. A covering of scales is PATO_0001804 scaly.
Lobed like a comb, with narrow, closely set, parallel divisions, matches the definition of FLOPO:0991033 pectinate.

target: abruptly narrowed (FLOPO:0991316) [bearer: plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023]
reason: The bearer is the apex and the quality is the existing value FLOPO:0991316 abruptly narrowed.
In these descriptions 'lutescent' means yellowish. The '-ish' hedge goes in the record as an approximate value (pattern 01), not in a new colour term.
'Sub-' makes it an approximate value of ovate, and 'broadly' qualifies the proportions. Neither needs a new term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (transition between two values: ovate FLOPO:0991024 – orbicular PATO_0001934)
reason: A hyphenated compound of two shapes, like 'oblong-ovate': a shape between ovate and round.

Palmately nerved = three or more primary veins diverging radially from one point, which is the definition of PATO_0001967 actinodromous. In '3- to 7-palminerved' the number is a count of parts (pattern 03).
'Without resin' and 'sin fluido resinoso' negate FLOPO:0991075 resinous. Resin is a substance, not a part, so an entity-absence rule does not fit.
A corolline perigone or flower has a perianth that looks like a corolla: thin, soft and coloured. That is FLOPO:0991141 petaloid.
Involucral bracts of unequal width are a set of like parts differing in size, which is the definition of FLOPO:0991101 unequal. The dimension (width, PATO_0000921) can be kept in the record.
Penicillate (misspelt here) style branches end in a tuft of hairs like a brush, which matches PATO_0002315 brush-like shape.
This is a part extracted as a quality. 'Without androecia' is an absence (pattern 15), and 'stamens unknown' states no quality at all.
A lateral leaflet whose base is inequilateral has two sides of different size. The definition note of FLOPO:0991101 unequal names 'the two sides of a leaf base' explicitly.

This is a length of a part, not a quality, and the part is ambiguous: a grass floret callus, an orchid lip callus and a petiole callus are different structures. The only PO class, PO_0005052 plant callus, is wound or culture tissue and would ground all of them wrongly.
